The italic alphabet, and the letter Unicode never encoded

There is a hole in this alphabet and it has a good reason. When Unicode encoded the mathematical italic letters at U+1D434 it left out lowercase h, because ℎ was already in the standard as the Planck constant and the rule is never to encode the same character twice. The h you paste from here is that borrowed one. Everything else is a purpose-made italic character rather than a slant applied to normal text by a font.

Italic earns its place where you would normally reach for emphasis and cannot: a film title inside a chat message, a quoted line in a Discord post, one word in a forum reply that should read as an aside. Numbers are the thing to watch. No italic digit set exists, so a date or a price in the middle of the line reverts to upright figures and the join is visible.

Where Italic text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks in most bios, posts, display names and chat — X, Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Reddit. Watch outRefused by real-name fields (Facebook, LinkedIn's name field) and unsearchable: these are separate characters from ordinary letters, so nobody will find you by typing your name.

Italic questions

Why does the lowercase h look different from the rest?

Because it is a different character with a different history. Unicode had already encoded ℎ at U+210E for the Planck constant before the mathematical italic run existed, and it does not duplicate characters, so no italic h was added at U+1D455. Fonts draw the two from separate designs, which is why the h can sit slightly off.

Can I get italic numbers?

Not in this style. Unicode never encoded an italic digit run, so numerals stay plain here no matter what you type. If a line is mostly figures and you want them styled, bold, sans-serif, monospace and double-struck all have their own digits and will keep a phone number or a price consistent.

Is this the same as pressing Ctrl and I?

No. A word processor keeps your letters and tells the renderer to slant them, so the slant vanishes if the formatting is stripped. Here the letters themselves are swapped for different characters. That is why it survives a paste into a field with no formatting at all, and also why search cannot match it.
